statement: For a unit-free canonical ordinary CNF with m clauses and L literal occurrences, eliminate pivot x with p positive and q negative pivot clauses, d=p+q, retained-clause literal mass R, and pivot-tail masses U_plus,U_minus. Before tautology removal/dedup/subsumption, post-elimination literal mass satisfies L'<=R+q*U_plus+p*U_minus. For a mixed pivot and k=max(p,q), since R>=2(m-d), L'<=k(L-d)-2(k-1)(m-d). Canonicalization can only decrease L'. For a pure pivot there are no resolvents and L'=R<=L-d.
proof: The input literal mass decomposes exactly as L=R+d+U_plus+U_minus.

Each positive tail participates in q raw resolvents and each negative tail participates in p raw resolvents. A resolvent union has width no larger than the sum of its parent-tail widths, hence total resolvent literal mass is at most q*U_plus+p*U_minus.
For a mixed pivot let k=max(p,q). Then q*U_plus+p*U_minus<=k(U_plus+U_minus)=k(L-d-R), so L'<=k(L-d)-(k-1)R.
At an ordinary unit-free elimination stage every retained clause has width at least two, and there are m-d retained clauses, so R>=2(m-d). Therefore L'<=k(L-d)-2(k-1)(m-d).
If one polarity bucket is empty, no resolvents are created and the exact deletion-only bound L'=R<=L-d applies.
All bounds are pre-canonicalization; tautology removal, duplicate collapse, subsumption and unit propagation cannot increase literal mass.
relation_to_previous: C025_DEGREE4_BALANCED_SURVIVAL_LITERAL_TRANSPORT is the N54 d=4,p=q=2 specialization of this general bound combined with root equality L=36 and retained width floor.
